However, one who does not lay tefillin for appetite — such as one who follows his business — is fit to write, as we say regarding slaughter that he is called a valid slaughterer; and so from Ran's words, he disqualifies only one who casts off the yoke, abandons the permitted and eats the forbidden. Ran wrote he is disqualified only rabbinically, for biblically an apostate for idolatry is not an apostate for the entire Torah — and this requires study. In Yoreh De'ah siman 2 s.b. Ran ruled that out of spite his law is like a gentile; and one could say here it discusses one who does not act out of spite and also not for appetite — for in Avodah Zarah ch. 2 Ran wrote: if permitted and forbidden are before him and he leaves the permitted and eats the forbidden, he is called acting out of spite; and there he ruled that out of spite is a sectarian, and if he wrote a Torah scroll it is burned — therefore one must say here it discusses not out of spite; if so, how did he write that he abandons the permitted and eats forbidden, which would be out of spite for him? One must say: in Gittin it discusses one who explicitly states he does not act out of spite but for the taste of the forbidden; or in Gittin he ate once and in Avodah Zarah he ate many times, tasting forbidden the first time — so Tosafos in Avodah Zarah and so in the Gemara, all per Ran. But per Rashba and Tur and Yoreh De'ah ibid., out of spite for one matter is not suspected for the entire Torah; and Chullin implies their view, for it labors to establish "apostate" for what, and not to establish "apostate out of spite" — and this requires study on Rabbeinu Yerucham in Yoreh De'ah siman 258, who wrote out of spite is a sectarian and if he wrote a Torah scroll it is burned, like Rashi Avodah Zarah 26 — if so, necessarily here it discusses one who does not act out of spite, yet here it writes it discusses one who acts out of spite — requires study. In Tosafos ibid. s.v. "remove from here," etc., it implies even for appetite he is invalid to write a Torah scroll:

(Seif katan 2) A Kuti, etc. So it should read, for an idolater is invalid in any case, etc., as written in siman 32 seif 9, and even a Jew standing over him does not help according to Rambam. In Eliyah Rabbah, in the name of his son Maharash, he asked: Tosafot in Menachot 42, s.v. ve'el, ask regarding the baraita in Gittin: a Sefer Torah, tefillin, or mezuzah written by a min, informer, idolater, slave, woman, minor, Kuti, or apostate is invalid. Regarding an idolater, let it derive from the fact that he does not write lishmah. Tosafot answered: it was needed because of slave and woman, etc.; although it taught idolater, so too it taught Kuti, even though ordinarily he writes for Mount Gerizim, end quote. Thus Tosafot answered that it mentioned idolater because of the others; if so, why did Magen Avraham erase it? In Shulchan Aruch too one could say that it used the language of the baraita because of the others. This is the substance of his expanded question. In my humble opinion, he understood that before Magen Avraham both words were written, idolater and Kuti, and Magen Avraham erased idolater and retained only Kuti. If so, the author of Eliyah Rabbah would have asked well. But in truth, before Magen Avraham his version had only idolater and not Kuti. Therefore it was reasonable to Magen Avraham that this came from a printer's error, for such is the way of printers with such words, and instead of idolater it should read Kuti. For we see that in any case he did not copy the entire language of the baraita, for even if we read idolater, he omitted Kuti, which is mentioned in the baraita. If so, it is preferable to him to say it should read Kuti, so we need not say "because of the others." What Eliyah Rabbah wrote further, that Tosafot also wrote regarding a Kuti that he writes for Mount Gerizim and is worse than an idolater: in my humble opinion, Tosafot in Avodah Zarah 27 also wrote as in Menachot but did not conclude by bringing proof from the fact that it taught Kuti, that ordinarily he writes for Mount Gerizim. That is because one can say the baraita speaks before they found the image of a dove on Mount Gerizim, as stated in the first chapter of Chullin 6, but that this tanna holds like the view that Kutim were lion converts; and so Rashi and Ran explicitly wrote in Gittin. If so, it does not appear regarding them that ordinarily it is for Mount Gerizim. Magen Avraham holds that nevertheless he acts lishmah and his law is like an apostate Jew, who is not subject to the mitzvah of tying. Although for us, after they found the image of a dove, they are like complete idolaters, as stated in Chullin, and so we rule in Yoreh De'ah siman 2 seif 8, nevertheless there is no further difficulty on Beit Yosef here in Shulchan Aruch, who copied Kuti; for according to us he is in any case invalid because he writes for Mount Gerizim. One can say he used the language of the baraita, which speaks before they found the image of a dove, so it should read.
Even according to Rosh, who is lenient regarding processing, that is when a Jew stands over him. He establishes it as a convert who returned to his former ways, for in Gittin 45b the baraita teaches: there was an incident with one idolater in Sidon who wrote a Sefer Torah, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permitted buying it from him. The Talmud asks: but Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel requires processing lishmah; all the more he requires writing lishmah, and an idolater does not act lishmah. It answers that the above idolater of Sidon was not an actual idolater, but a convert who returned to his former ways out of fear, meaning, as Rashi explains, so idolaters would not kill him, and such a person acts lishmah. According to Rosh, it would have been better to establish it as an actual idolater with a Jew standing over him. Rather, necessarily, regarding writing Rosh agrees that this does not help. See what I will write, with God's help, in seif katan 7.

biur_halacha.he: שכתבם אפיקורס - הוא האדוק לעבודת כוכבים כן איתא בב"י בשם רש"י ובכ"מ ברמב"ם הלכות תפילין פ"א הי"ג לאפוקי ממה שהוגה באיזה דפוס ברש"י גיטין מ"ה ע"ב אפיקורס יהודי שאינו מאמין לדברי רז"ל שזה אינו מפירש"י כידוע הגם שלענינים אחרים ג"ז הוא בכלל אפיקורס אבל לא לענין זה דישרף. ולענין דינא סופר כזה נ"ל פשוט דצריך לגנוז פרשיותיו דשמא לא עיבד הקלף לשמה ושמא לא כתב הפרשיות והאזכרות לשמה ושמא לא היה זהיר בדין חק תוכות כיון דאינו מאמין בדחז"ל וגם חשוד הוא להכשיל לאחרים מיהו אי איתרמי שעמדו אחרים ע"ג וראו שנעשה הכל כהלכה כגון שהוא לא כתב אלא איזו אותיות בהפרשיות אלו בפניהם או בהיריעות של הס"ת אפ"ה יש לעיין אם איש כזה הוא בכלל בר קשירה ולכאורה יש להביא ראיה להתיר דהלא לענין זביחה ג"כ מידריש מי שהוא בכלל בר זביחה אכול מזבחו ולא ממי שאינו בר זביחה וכדאיתא בחולין ג' ע"ב תוד"ה קסבר ואפ"ה פסק ביו"ד סימן ב' ס"ט דצדוקי וביתוסי אם נבדק סכינם ואחרים עומדים על גבם שחיטתם כשרה אלמא דכיון דאחזיק במצוה זו אף דלא כתיבה קרינן בהו שהם בני זביחה ומאמינים במצות זביחה וכדפירש הפמ"ג שם עי"ש א"כ ה"נ בעניננו לכאורה אם אחרים עומדים ע"ג ורואין שלא היה בו חסרון דחק תוכות שמצוי מאד במלאכת הכתיבה וגם שנכתב לשמה אין לפוסלו דהוי עדיין בכלל בר קשירה אבל יש לדחות דהלא ידוע דאם שביק התירא ואכיל איסורא אף בדבר אחד תו הוי בכלל אפיקורס ואנשים כאלו בזמנינו ידוע שאינם חוששין כלל למצות ומצוי אצלם חילול שבת בפרהסיא ג"כ וא"כ דינם כמו שמסיק הש"ך שם לענין קראים ע"כ יותר טוב שימחקם ויכתוב אחרים תחתיהם אך אם אינו יכול למחקם מחמת כסדרן או באותיות השם צ"ע למעשה:
biur_halacha.en: That an apikores wrote them - This refers to one attached to idolatry; so it is stated in Beit Yosef in the name of Rashi, and in Kesef Mishneh on Rambam, Hilchot Tefillin 1:13, excluding what was emended in some printings of Rashi, Gittin 45b, "a Jewish apikores who does not believe the words of Chazal," for that is not from Rashi's commentary, as is known. Although for other matters this too is included in apikores, it is not so for this matter, that they must be burned. As to the practical law, it appears simple to me that a scribe such as this requires genizah for his parshiyot, lest he did not process the parchment lishmah, lest he did not write the parshiyot and Divine Names lishmah, and lest he was not careful about the law of chak tokhot, since he does not believe in the words of Chazal; he is also suspected of causing others to stumble. However, if it happened that others stood over him and saw that everything was done according to halachah, for example he wrote only some letters in these parshiyot before them, or in sheets of a Sefer Torah, even so one must consider whether such a person is included among those subject to the mitzvah of tying. At first glance there is proof to permit, for regarding slaughter too we expound that one who is included in slaughter, "eat of his slaughter," but not one who is not included in slaughter, as in Chullin 3b, Tosafot s.v. kasavar; nevertheless in Yoreh De'ah siman 2 seif 9 it is ruled that a Sadducee or Boethusian, if his knife was checked and others stand over him, his slaughter is kosher. Thus, since he is established with regard to this mitzvah, even though it is not written, we call him among those who are capable of slaughter and who believe in the mitzvah of slaughter, as Peri Megadim explains there, see there. If so, here too in our case, apparently if others stand over him and see that there was no defect of chak tokhot, which is very common in the writing work, and also that it was written lishmah, one should not disqualify it, for he is still included in the mitzvah of tying. But this can be rejected, for it is known that if one abandons the permitted and eats the forbidden, even in one matter, he is thereby included as an apikores; and such people in our time are known not to be concerned for mitzvot at all, and public Shabbat desecration is also common among them. If so, their law is as Shach concludes there regarding Karaites. Therefore it is better that he erase them and write others in their place; but if he cannot erase them because of kesidran or in the letters of the Divine Name, this requires study in practice.
